title: Separatedness from pairwise affine separated neighbourhoods
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose that for every pair of affine open subschemes $A,B\subseteq X$ there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $A\cup B$ such that $W$ is separated over $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, meaning that $\Delta_W:W\to W\times_S W$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_SX$ is a closed immersion. Consequently $X$ is separated and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. There is no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $X$ or on the witnessing opens $W$.

source.place: Tag 0AP6, paragraph following definition-ind-quasi-affine: separatedness from a separated open containing each pair of affine opens; explicit absolute-diagonal formulation

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, $Y=X\times_SX$, with projections $p,q$. For each pair of affine opens $A,B$ choose a witnessing separated open $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $W\times_SW$ is the open $p^{-1}W\cap q^{-1}W$ in $Y$. These opens cover $Y$: for $y\in Y$, choose affine neighbourhoods $A$ of $p(y)$ and $B$ of $q(y)$; their witness contains both projections, hence $y$. For each such open take an affine open cover, which exists since it is a scheme. Together these give an affine open cover $(T_i)$ of $Y$, each $T_i$ contained in one $W\times_SW$.

source.place: Tag 0AP6, paragraph after definition-ind-quasi-affine; Schemes Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product

proof.text: Fix one witness $W$. The inverse image of $W\times_SW=p^{-1}W\cap q^{-1}W$ under $\Delta_X$ is exactly $W$, since $p\Delta_X=q\Delta_X=\mathrm{id}_X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] it is the pullback open subscheme. Its map to $W\times_SW$ is $\Delta_W$: both projections are the identity on $W$, so uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the maps. Thus for $T_i\subseteq W\times_SW$, the restricted morphisms $\Delta_X^{-1}(T_i)\to T_i$ and $\Delta_W^{-1}(T_i)\to T_i$ are identical, including their structure-sheaf maps.

source.place: Schemes Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product, applied to the diagonal; explicit universal-property calculation

proof.text: The hypothesis says $\Delta_W$ is a closed immersion. Apply part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] to the affine open $T_i$ of $W\times_SW$. Its inverse image is affine and the induced ring map on sections is surjective. Step 2 supplies exactly these assertions for $\Delta_X$ over $T_i$. Since the $T_i$ cover $Y$, part (2) of the same cited criterion proves that $\Delta_X$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, (1) implies (2) and (3) implies (1)

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], the closed-immersion assertion for $\Delta_X$ means that $X\to S$ is separated. Apply [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] to this structure morphism to conclude that it is quasi-separated, hence $X$ is quasi-separated. Every cover above may be infinite; no step takes a finite subcover or assumes $X$ or $W$ quasi-compact.

The statement is true: it is the general form of the Stacks argument in more-morphisms.tex:19528-19534 (Tag 0AP6, paragraph after definition-ind-quasi-affine) that a scheme is separated when every two affine opens lie in a separated open. It assumes no quasi-compactness. Its stmt_deps match the notions it uses. The only citer, lem-a1-ind-quasi-affine-permanence (clause 3, with W = A ∪ B quasi-affine), uses exactly this hypothesis. No duplicate found: grep over the DAG and blueprint_refs search turned up nothing with the same content. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product applies with U = S (Tag 01JR, schemes.tex:3196). The opens p^-1W ∩ q^-1W cover X ×_S X by choosing affine neighbourhoods of the two projections of a point; affine covers of these opens give the affine cover T_i. Step 2 (marked elementary): Δ_X^-1(W ×_S W) = W, and the restriction of Δ_X is Δ_W by uniqueness in the fibre product, via the open-preimage pullback lemma. Step 3: parts (1) and (2) of lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion apply as stated (Tag 01QO, morphisms.tex:56, (1)⇒(2) and (3)⇒(1)). Step 4: separated holds by def-weil-proper-morphism and quasi-separated by lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated. Edge cases checked: empty X, affine X, infinite disjoint unions, and the doubled-origin line (the hypothesis correctly fails). I accept the four declared generic tool uses, all Mathlib-status scheme lemmas. No SGA source is cited. No changes.
